mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen monotonically from -21.6% to -9.6% over four weeks, signaling workplace reopening. This sustained recovery in commuting activity will drive retail-and-recreation footfall upward over the next four weeks as workers resume shopping and leisure trips near employment centers.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 12 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed RETAIL_REC mean over last 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses to below -15% in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized at elevated levels (22.4% to 27.0%), indicating sustained essential-goods shopping behavior. This persistent demand signal reflects consumer confidence and mobility willingness that will extend into discretionary retail-and-recreation categories over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 2.9 points week-on-week to t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 20% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not improve in weeks t+1 and t+2.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has improved from -20.7% to -14.0% over four weeks. When transit recovery exceeds -15%, it signals sufficient public mobility infrastructure utilization to enable retail-and-recreation trips. This threshold crossing will drive RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -14.0% at t-0w, crossing -15% threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over next 28 days does not exceed last 28-day mean, or TRANSIT falls back below -15% within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 10.9% to 7.3% over four weeks, indicating reduced home confinement. Simultaneously, RETAIL_REC has improved from -21.4% to -17.7%. The joint signal of declining residential time and rising retail mobility reflects a behavioral shift toward out-of-home activity that will accelerate RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks when both proxies interact.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines below 8% and RETAIL_REC improves week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 3.6 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL does not continue declining or RETAIL_REC reverses to -19% or lower in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has deteriorated from -14.9% to -27.0% then recovered to -17.1%, indicating volatile outdoor-activity restrictions or behavioral avoidance. When PARKS mobility is suppressed below -20%, it signals active mobility constraints that redirect consumer activity away from outdoor retail-recreation venues, depressing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached -27.0% at t-1w, indicating constraint regime
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over next 14 days despite PARKS remaining below -20%, or PARKS recovers above -15% within one week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES have both improved steadily over four weeks (TRANSIT: -20.7% to -14.0%; WORKPLACES: -21.6% to -9.6%), signaling a synchronized reopening regime. When both mobility streams improve together, it indicates seasonal or policy-driven expansion of economic activity that will lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks through complementary effects.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series show monotonic improvement over four weeks
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 3 points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not exceed -15% in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC show divergent trends: grocery mobility is elevated and rising (+27.0%), while retail-recreation remains suppressed (-17.7%). This divergence indicates consumers are prioritizing essential shopping over discretionary retail. The gap will narrow over the next two weeks as essential-goods confidence spills over into retail-recreation categories.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 25% while RETAIL_REC remains below -15%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in weeks t+1 and t+2, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 20%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 10.9% to 7.3%, indicating reduced home time. In a reopening regime where outdoor restrictions are easing (PARKS recovery from -27.0% to -17.1%), declining residential confinement will drive consumers toward retail-and-recreation venues over the next week as the primary outlet for released mobility demand.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 8% and PARKS improves above -20%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in week t+1, or RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 9% within one week.
